timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

  export const meta = {

    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

cells.source: # Baseline -- Convolutional Neural Network on MNIST
## Imports

import os
import time

import numpy as np
import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F

if torch.cuda.is_available():
    torch.backends.cudnn.deterministic = True
## Settings

##########################
### SETTINGS
##########################

# Device
device = torch.device("cuda:0" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu")

# Hyperparameters
random_seed = 1
learning_rate = 0.001
num_epochs = 10
batch_size = 128

# Architecture
num_classes = 10
## Dataset
#!pip install gitpython

import os

from git import Repo

if not os.path.exists("mnist-pngs"):
    Repo.clone_from("https://github.com/rasbt/mnist-pngs", "mnist-pngs")

from torchvision import transforms

data_transforms = {
    "train": transforms.Compose(
        [
            transforms.Resize(32),
            transforms.RandomCrop((28, 28)),
            transforms.ToTensor(),
            # normalize images to [-1, 1] range
            transforms.Normalize((0.5, 0.5, 0.5), (0.5, 0.5, 0.5)),
        ]
    ),
    "test": transforms.Compose(
        [
            transforms.Resize(32),
            transforms.CenterCrop((28, 28)),
            transforms.ToTensor(),
            # normalize images to [-1, 1] range
            transforms.Normalize((0.5, 0.5, 0.5), (0.5, 0.5, 0.5)),
        ]
    ),
}

from torch.utils.data.dataset import random_split
from torchvision.datasets import ImageFolder

train_dset = ImageFolder(root="mnist-pngs/train", transform=data_transforms["train"])

train_dset, valid_dset = random_split(train_dset, lengths=[55000, 5000])

test_dset = ImageFolder(root="mnist-pngs/test", transform=data_transforms["test"])

from torch.utils.data import DataLoader

train_loader = DataLoader(
    dataset=train_dset,
    batch_size=batch_size,
    drop_last=True,
    num_workers=4,
    shuffle=True,
)

valid_loader = DataLoader(
    dataset=valid_dset,
    batch_size=batch_size,
    drop_last=False,
    num_workers=4,
    shuffle=False,
)

test_loader = DataLoader(
    dataset=test_dset,
    batch_size=batch_size,
    drop_last=False,
    num_workers=4,
    shuffle=False,
)

%matplotlib inline
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import torchvision.utils as vutils

real_batch = next(iter(train_loader))
plt.figure(figsize=(8, 8))
plt.axis("off")
plt.title("Training images")
plt.imshow(
    np.transpose(
        vutils.make_grid(real_batch[0][:64], padding=2, normalize=True), (1, 2, 0)
    )
)
plt.show()

cells.source: ## Model

import torch


class PyTorchCNN(torch.nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, num_classes):
        super().__init__()

        self.num_classes = num_classes
        self.features = torch.nn.Sequential(
            torch.nn.Conv2d(
                in_channels=3,
                out_channels=8,
                kernel_size=(3, 3),
                stride=(1, 1),
                padding=1,
            ),
            torch.nn.ReLU(),
            torch.nn.MaxPool2d(kernel_size=(2, 2), stride=(2, 2), padding=0),
            torch.nn.ReLU(),
            torch.nn.Conv2d(
                in_channels=8,
                out_channels=16,
                kernel_size=(3, 3),
                stride=(1, 1),
                padding=1,
            ),
            torch.nn.ReLU(),
            torch.nn.MaxPool2d(kernel_size=(2, 2), stride=(2, 2), padding=0),
        )

        self.classifier = torch.nn.Sequential(
            torch.nn.Flatten(),
            torch.nn.Linear(784, 128),
            torch.nn.ReLU(),
            torch.nn.Linear(128, num_classes),
        )

    def forward(self, x):
        x = self.features(x)
        x = self.classifier(x)
        return x


torch.manual_seed(random_seed)
model = PyTorchCNN(num_classes=num_classes)
model = model.to(device)
## Training

def compute_accuracy(model, data_loader, device):
    with torch.no_grad():
        correct_pred, num_examples = 0, 0
        for features, targets in data_loader:
            features, targets = features.to(device), targets.to(device)
            logits = model(features)
            _, predicted_labels = torch.max(logits, 1)
            num_examples += targets.size(0)
            correct_pred += (predicted_labels == targets).sum()
        return correct_pred.float() / num_examples

optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=learning_rate)

start_time = time.time()
for epoch in range(num_epochs):
    model = model.train()
    for batch_idx, (features, targets) in enumerate(train_loader):

        features, targets = features.to(device), targets.to(device)

        ### Forward pass
        logits = model(features)
        loss = F.cross_entropy(logits, targets)

        ### Backward pass (backpropagation)
        optimizer.zero_grad()
        loss.backward()

        ### Update model parameters
        optimizer.step()

        ### Batch-level logging
        if not (batch_idx + 1) % 100:
            print(
                f"Epoch: {epoch + 1:03d}/{num_epochs:03d} | "
                f"Batch: {batch_idx + 1:03d}/{len(train_loader):03d} | "
                f"Loss: {loss:.4f}"
            )

    ### Epoch-level logging
    model = model.eval()
    train_acc = compute_accuracy(model, train_loader, device)
    valid_acc = compute_accuracy(model, valid_loader, device)
    print(
        f"Training accuracy: {train_acc * 100:.2f}% | "
        f"Validation accuracy: {valid_acc * 100:.2f}%"
    )
    print(f"Time elapsed: {(time.time() - start_time) / 60:.2f} min")

print(f"Total training time: {(time.time() - start_time) / 60:.2f} min")

## Imports

import os
import time

import numpy as np
import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F

if torch.cuda.is_available():
    torch.backends.cudnn.deterministic = True
## Settings

##########################
### SETTINGS
##########################

# Hyperparameters
RANDOM_SEED = 1
LEARNING_RATE = 0.001
NUM_EPOCHS = 10
BATCH_SIZE = 128

# Architecture
NUM_CLASSES = 10
## Dataset
#!pip install gitpython

import os

from git import Repo

if not os.path.exists("mnist-pngs"):
    Repo.clone_from("https://github.com/rasbt/mnist-pngs", "mnist-pngs")

from torchvision import transforms

data_transforms = {
    "train": transforms.Compose(
        [
            transforms.Resize(32),
            transforms.RandomCrop((28, 28)),
            transforms.ToTensor(),
            # normalize images to [-1, 1] range
            transforms.Normalize((0.5, 0.5, 0.5), (0.5, 0.5, 0.5)),
        ]
    ),
    "test": transforms.Compose(
        [
            transforms.Resize(32),
            transforms.CenterCrop((28, 28)),
            transforms.ToTensor(),
            # normalize images to [-1, 1] range
            transforms.Normalize((0.5, 0.5, 0.5), (0.5, 0.5, 0.5)),
        ]
    ),
}

from torch.utils.data.dataset import random_split
from torchvision.datasets import ImageFolder

train_dset = ImageFolder(root="mnist-pngs/train", transform=data_transforms["train"])

train_dset, valid_dset = random_split(train_dset, lengths=[55000, 5000])

test_dset = ImageFolder(root="mnist-pngs/test", transform=data_transforms["test"])

from torch.utils.data import DataLoader

train_loader = DataLoader(
    dataset=train_dset,
    batch_size=BATCH_SIZE,
    drop_last=True,
    num_workers=4,
    shuffle=True,
)

valid_loader = DataLoader(
    dataset=valid_dset,
    batch_size=BATCH_SIZE,
    drop_last=False,
    num_workers=4,
    shuffle=False,
)

test_loader = DataLoader(
    dataset=test_dset,
    batch_size=BATCH_SIZE,
    drop_last=False,
    num_workers=4,
    shuffle=False,
)

%matplotlib inline
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import torchvision.utils as vutils

real_batch = next(iter(train_loader))
plt.figure(figsize=(8, 8))
plt.axis("off")
plt.title("Training images")
plt.imshow(
    np.transpose(
        vutils.make_grid(real_batch[0][:64], padding=2, normalize=True), (1, 2, 0)
    )
)
plt.show()

import torch


class PyTorchCNN(torch.nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, num_classes):
        super().__init__()

        self.num_classes = num_classes
        self.features = torch.nn.Sequential(
            torch.nn.Conv2d(
                in_channels=3,
                out_channels=8,
                kernel_size=(3, 3),
                stride=(1, 1),
                padding=1,
            ),
            torch.nn.ReLU(),
            torch.nn.MaxPool2d(kernel_size=(2, 2), stride=(2, 2), padding=0),
            torch.nn.ReLU(),
            torch.nn.Conv2d(
                in_channels=8,
                out_channels=16,
                kernel_size=(3, 3),
                stride=(1, 1),
                padding=1,
            ),
            torch.nn.ReLU(),
            torch.nn.MaxPool2d(kernel_size=(2, 2), stride=(2, 2), padding=0),
        )

        self.classifier = torch.nn.Sequential(
            torch.nn.Flatten(),
            torch.nn.Linear(784, 128),
            torch.nn.ReLU(),
            torch.nn.Linear(128, num_classes),
        )

    def forward(self, x):
        x = self.features(x)
        x = self.classifier(x)
        return x

import pytorch_lightning as pl
import torchmetrics

    def __init__(self, model, learning_rate):

        # The inherited PyTorch module

        # Save settings and hyperparameters to the log directory

        self.valid_acc = torchmetrics.Accuracy()
        self.test_acc = torchmetrics.Accuracy()

        return self.model(x)

    def _shared_step(self, batch):
        features, true_labels = batch
        logits = self(features)
        loss = torch.nn.functional.cross_entropy(logits, true_labels)
        predicted_labels = torch.argmax(logits, dim=1)

        return loss, true_labels, predicted_labels

    def training_step(self, batch, batch_idx):
        loss, true_labels, predicted_labels = self._shared_step(batch)
        self.log("train_loss", loss)

        # To account for Dropout behavior during evaluation
        self.model.eval()
        with torch.no_grad():
            _, true_labels, predicted_labels = self._shared_step(batch)
        self.train_acc.update(predicted_labels, true_labels)
        self.log("train_acc", self.train_acc, on_epoch=True, on_step=False)
        self.model.train()
        return loss  # this is passed to the optimzer for training

    def validation_step(self, batch, batch_idx):
        loss, true_labels, predicted_labels = self._shared_step(batch)
        self.log("valid_loss", loss)
        self.valid_acc(predicted_labels, true_labels)
        self.log(
            "valid_acc", self.valid_acc, on_epoch=True, on_step=False, prog_bar=True
        )

    def test_step(self, batch, batch_idx):
        loss, true_labels, predicted_labels = self._shared_step(batch)
        self.test_acc(predicted_labels, true_labels)

from pytorch_lightning.loggers import CSVLogger

torch.manual_seed(RANDOM_SEED)
pytorch_model = PyTorchCNN(num_classes=NUM_CLASSES)

lightning_model = LightningModel(model=pytorch_model, learning_rate=LEARNING_RATE)

callbacks = [
    ModelCheckpoint(save_top_k=1, mode="max", monitor="valid_acc"),  # save top 1 model
    pl.callbacks.progress.TQDMProgressBar(refresh_rate=50),
]

logger = CSVLogger(save_dir="logs/", name="my-model")

import time

trainer = pl.Trainer(
    max_epochs=NUM_EPOCHS,
    callbacks=callbacks,
    accelerator="auto",  # Uses GPUs or TPUs if available
    devices="auto",  # Uses all available GPUs/TPUs if applicable
    logger=logger,
    log_every_n_steps=100,
)

start_time = time.time()
trainer.fit(
    model=lightning_model, train_dataloaders=train_loader, val_dataloaders=valid_loader
)

runtime = (time.time() - start_time) / 60
print(f"Training took {runtime:.2f} min in total.")

        predicted_labels = torch.argmax(logits, dim=1)

        return loss, true_labels, predicted_labels

    def training_step(self, batch, batch_idx):
        loss, true_labels, predicted_labels = self._shared_step(batch)
        self.log("train_loss", loss)

        # To account for Dropout behavior during evaluation
        self.model.eval()
        with torch.no_grad():
            _, true_labels, predicted_labels = self._shared_step(batch)
        self.train_acc.update(predicted_labels, true_labels)
        self.log("train_acc", self.train_acc, on_epoch=True, on_step=False)
        self.model.train()
        return loss  # this is passed to the optimzer for training

    def validation_step(self, batch, batch_idx):
        loss, true_labels, predicted_labels = self._shared_step(batch)
        self.log("valid_loss", loss)
        self.valid_acc(predicted_labels, true_labels)
        self.log(
            "valid_acc", self.valid_acc, on_epoch=True, on_step=False, prog_bar=True
        )

    def test_step(self, batch, batch_idx):
        loss, true_labels, predicted_labels = self._shared_step(batch)
        self.test_acc(predicted_labels, true_labels)
        self.log("test_acc", self.test_acc, on_epoch=True, on_step=False)

    def configure_optimizers(self):
        optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(self.parameters(), lr=self.learning_rate)
        return optimizer</cell id="cell-15">

<cell id="cell-23">import torch


class PyTorchCNN(torch.nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, num_classes):
        super().__init__()

        self.num_classes = num_classes
        self.features = torch.nn.Sequential(
            torch.nn.Conv2d(
                in_channels=3,
                out_channels=8,
                kernel_size=(3, 3),
                stride=(1, 1),
                padding=1,
            ),
            torch.nn.ReLU(),
            torch.nn.MaxPool2d(kernel_size=(2, 2), stride=(2, 2), padding=0),
            torch.nn.ReLU(),
            torch.nn.Conv2d(
                in_channels=8,
                out_channels=16,
                kernel_size=(3, 3),
                stride=(1, 1),
                padding=1,
            ),
            torch.nn.ReLU(),
            torch.nn.MaxPool2d(kernel_size=(2, 2), stride=(2, 2), padding=0),
        )

        self.classifier = torch.nn.Sequential(
            torch.nn.Flatten(),
            torch.nn.Linear(784, 128),
            torch.nn.ReLU(),
            torch.nn.Linear(128, num_classes),
        )

    def forward(self, x):
        x = self.features(x)
        x = self.classifier(x)
        return x</cell id="cell-23">
<cell id="cell-24">import pytorch_lightning as pl
import torchmetrics


# LightningModule that receives a PyTorch model as input
class LightningModel(pl.LightningModule):
    def __init__(self, model, learning_rate):
        super().__init__()

        self.learning_rate = learning_rate
        # The inherited PyTorch module
        self.model = model

        # Save settings and hyperparameters to the log directory
        # but skip the model parameters
        self.save_hyperparameters(ignore=["model"])

        # Set up attributes for computing the accuracy
        self.train_acc = torchmetrics.Accuracy()
        self.valid_acc = torchmetrics.Accuracy()
        self.test_acc = torchmetrics.Accuracy()

    # Defining the forward method is only necessary
    # if you want to use a Trainer's .predict() method (optional)
    def forward(self, x):
        return self.model(x)

    # A common forward step to compute the loss and labels
    # this is used for training, validation, and testing below
    def _shared_step(self, batch):
        features, true_labels = batch
        logits = self(features)
        loss = torch.nn.functional.cross_entropy(logits, true_labels)
        predicted_labels = torch.argmax(logits, dim=1)

        return loss, true_labels, predicted_labels

    def training_step(self, batch, batch_idx):
        loss, true_labels, predicted_labels = self._shared_step(batch)
        self.log("train_loss", loss)

        # To account for Dropout behavior during evaluation
        self.model.eval()
        with torch.no_grad():
            _, true_labels, predicted_labels = self._shared_step(batch)
        self.train_acc.update(predicted_labels, true_labels)
        self.log("train_acc", self.train_acc, on_epoch=True, on_step=False)
        self.model.train()
        return loss  # this is passed to the optimzer for training

    def validation_step(self, batch, batch_idx):
        loss, true_labels, predicted_labels = self._shared_step(batch)
        self.log("valid_loss", loss)
        self.valid_acc(predicted_labels, true_labels)
        self.log(
            "valid_acc", self.valid_acc, on_epoch=True, on_step=False, prog_bar=True
        )

    def test_step(self, batch, batch_idx):
        loss, true_labels, predicted_labels = self._shared_step(batch)
        self.test_acc(predicted_labels, true_labels)
        self.log("test_acc", self.test_acc, on_epoch=True, on_step=False)

    def configure_optimizers(self):
        optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(self.parameters(), lr=self.learning_rate)
        return optimizer</cell id="cell-24">

Also, since the k-fold approach doesn't use `validation_step` we can't checkpoint based on teh validation set accuracy and have the `training_accuracy` instead.</cell id="cell-26">

# K-Fold Cross-Validation Example -- Convolutional Neural Network on MNIST

This notebook shows how to apply k-fold cross-validation to deep neural networks using PyTorch Lightning and [`pl_cross`](https://github.com/SkafteNicki/pl_cross).

This notebook is based on a basic PyTorch Lightning notebook at [./baseline-cnn-mnist.ipynb](baseline-cnn-mnist.ipynb). The changes are annotated and/or highlighted.

    Repo.clone_from("https://github.com/rasbt/mnist-pngs", "mnist-pngs")

from torchvision import transforms

data_transforms = {
    "train": transforms.Compose(
        [
            transforms.Resize(32),
            transforms.RandomCrop((28, 28)),
            transforms.ToTensor(),
            # normalize images to [-1, 1] range
            transforms.Normalize((0.5, 0.5, 0.5), (0.5, 0.5, 0.5)),

        [
            transforms.Resize(32),
            transforms.CenterCrop((28, 28)),
            transforms.ToTensor(),
            # normalize images to [-1, 1] range
            transforms.Normalize((0.5, 0.5, 0.5), (0.5, 0.5, 0.5)),
        ]
    ),
}

from torch.utils.data.dataset import random_split
from torchvision.datasets import ImageFolder

train_dset = ImageFolder(root="mnist-pngs/train", transform=data_transforms["train"])

    dataset=train_dset,

cells.source: ## Model
The model setup is exactly as it is before, except that the current k-fold code won't be using `validation_step`. We can still leave it in the `LightningModule` as it doesn't hurt either.

import torch


class PyTorchCNN(torch.nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, num_classes):
        super().__init__()

        self.num_classes = num_classes
        self.features = torch.nn.Sequential(
            torch.nn.Conv2d(
                in_channels=3,
                out_channels=8,
                kernel_size=(3, 3),
                stride=(1, 1),
                padding=1,
            ),
            torch.nn.ReLU(),
            torch.nn.MaxPool2d(kernel_size=(2, 2), stride=(2, 2), padding=0),
            torch.nn.ReLU(),
            torch.nn.Conv2d(
                in_channels=8,
                out_channels=16,
                kernel_size=(3, 3),
                stride=(1, 1),
                padding=1,
            ),
            torch.nn.ReLU(),
            torch.nn.MaxPool2d(kernel_size=(2, 2), stride=(2, 2), padding=0),
        )

        self.classifier = torch.nn.Sequential(
            torch.nn.Flatten(),
            torch.nn.Linear(784, 128),
            torch.nn.ReLU(),
            torch.nn.Linear(128, num_classes),
        )

    def forward(self, x):
        x = self.features(x)
        x = self.classifier(x)
        return x

import pytorch_lightning as pl
import torchmetrics


# LightningModule that receives a PyTorch model as input
class LightningModel(pl.LightningModule):
    def __init__(self, model, learning_rate):
        super().__init__()

        self.learning_rate = learning_rate
        # The inherited PyTorch module
        self.model = model

        # Save settings and hyperparameters to the log directory
        # but skip the model parameters
        self.save_hyperparameters(ignore=["model"])

        # Set up attributes for computing the accuracy
        self.train_acc = torchmetrics.Accuracy()
        self.valid_acc = torchmetrics.Accuracy()
        self.test_acc = torchmetrics.Accuracy()

    # Defining the forward method is only necessary
    # if you want to use a Trainer's .predict() method (optional)
    def forward(self, x):
        return self.model(x)

    # A common forward step to compute the loss and labels
    # this is used for training, validation, and testing below
    def _shared_step(self, batch):
        features, true_labels = batch
        logits = self(features)
        loss = torch.nn.functional.cross_entropy(logits, true_labels)
        predicted_labels = torch.argmax(logits, dim=1)

        return loss, true_labels, predicted_labels

    def training_step(self, batch, batch_idx):
        loss, true_labels, predicted_labels = self._shared_step(batch)
        self.log("train_loss", loss)

        # To account for Dropout behavior during evaluation
        self.model.eval()
        with torch.no_grad():
            _, true_labels, predicted_labels = self._shared_step(batch)
        self.train_acc.update(predicted_labels, true_labels)
        self.log("train_acc", self.train_acc, on_epoch=True, on_step=False)
        self.model.train()
        return loss  # this is passed to the optimzer for training

    def validation_step(self, batch, batch_idx):
        loss, true_labels, predicted_labels = self._shared_step(batch)
        self.log("valid_loss", loss)
        self.valid_acc(predicted_labels, true_labels)
        self.log(
            "valid_acc", self.valid_acc, on_epoch=True, on_step=False, prog_bar=True
        )

    def test_step(self, batch, batch_idx):
        loss, true_labels, predicted_labels = self._shared_step(batch)
        self.test_acc(predicted_labels, true_labels)
        self.log("test_acc", self.test_acc, on_epoch=True, on_step=False)

    def configure_optimizers(self):
        optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(self.parameters(), lr=self.learning_rate)
        return optimizer
## Training

NEW: Note that for logging, we need to import a modified version of the logger from the `pl_cross` library. Also, since the k-fold approach doesn't use `validation_step` we can't checkpoint based on teh validation set accuracy and have the `training_accuracy` instead.

# OLD:
# from pytorch_lightning.loggers import CSVLogger
# NEW:
from pl_cross.loggers import CSVLogger
from pytorch_lightning.callbacks import ModelCheckpoint

torch.manual_seed(RANDOM_SEED)
pytorch_model = PyTorchCNN(num_classes=NUM_CLASSES)

lightning_model = LightningModel(model=pytorch_model, learning_rate=LEARNING_RATE)


# NEW: Kfold currently doesn't call model.validation_step()
# so the valid_acc tracking does unfortunately not work, and
# we have to change valid_acc to train_acc.

callbacks = [
    ModelCheckpoint(save_top_k=1, mode="max", monitor="train_acc"),  # save top 1 model
    pl.callbacks.progress.TQDMProgressBar(refresh_rate=50),
]

logger = CSVLogger(save_dir="logs/", name="my-kfold-model")
NEW: Instead of using `pl.Trainer`, we use the `Trainer` from the `pl_cross` library, which lets us specify the number of folds as shown below:

import time

# NEW:
from pl_cross import Trainer

trainer = Trainer(
    num_folds=5,
    shuffle=True,
    # stratified=True,
    max_epochs=NUM_EPOCHS,
    callbacks=callbacks,
    accelerator="auto",  # Uses GPUs or TPUs if available
    devices="auto",  # Uses all available GPUs/TPUs if applicable
    logger=logger,
    log_every_n_steps=100,
)

start_time = time.time()

# NEW
kfold_results = trainer.cross_validate(
    model=lightning_model,
    train_dataloader=train_loader,
)

runtime = (time.time() - start_time) / 60
print(f"Training took {runtime:.2f} min in total.")

<cell id="cell-13"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>## Model</cell id="cell-13">
<cell id="cell-14">import torch


class PyTorchCNN(torch.nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, num_classes):
        super().__init__()

        self.num_classes = num_classes
        self.features = torch.nn.Sequential(
            torch.nn.Conv2d(
                in_channels=3,
                out_channels=8,
                kernel_size=(3, 3),
                stride=(1, 1),
                padding=1,
            ),
            torch.nn.ReLU(),
            torch.nn.MaxPool2d(kernel_size=(2, 2), stride=(2, 2), padding=0),
            torch.nn.ReLU(),
            torch.nn.Conv2d(
                in_channels=8,
                out_channels=16,
                kernel_size=(3, 3),
                stride=(1, 1),
                padding=1,
            ),
            torch.nn.ReLU(),
            torch.nn.MaxPool2d(kernel_size=(2, 2), stride=(2, 2), padding=0),
        )

        self.classifier = torch.nn.Sequential(
            torch.nn.Flatten(),
            torch.nn.Linear(784, 128),
            torch.nn.ReLU(),
            torch.nn.Linear(128, num_classes),
        )

    def forward(self, x):
        x = self.features(x)
        x = self.classifier(x)
        return x


torch.manual_seed(random_seed)
model = PyTorchCNN(num_classes=num_classes)
model = model.to(device)</cell id="cell-14">
<cell id="cell-15"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>## Training</cell id="cell-15">
<cell id="cell-16">def compute_accuracy(model, data_loader, device):
    with torch.no_grad():
        correct_pred, num_examples = 0, 0
        for features, targets in data_loader:
            features, targets = features.to(device), targets.to(device)
            logits = model(features)
            _, predicted_labels = torch.max(logits, 1)
            num_examples += targets.size(0)
            correct_pred += (predicted_labels == targets).sum()
        return correct_pred.float() / num_examples</cell id="cell-16">
<cell id="cell-17">optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=learning_rate)

start_time = time.time()
for epoch in range(num_epochs):
    model = model.train()
    for batch_idx, (features, targets) in enumerate(train_loader):

        features, targets = features.to(device), targets.to(device)

        ### Forward pass
        logits = model(features)
        loss = F.cross_entropy(logits, targets)

        ### Backward pass (backpropagation)
        optimizer.zero_grad()
        loss.backward()

        ### Update model parameters
        optimizer.step()

        ### Batch-level logging
        if not (batch_idx + 1) % 100:
            print(
                f"Epoch: {epoch + 1:03d}/{num_epochs:03d} | "
                f"Batch: {batch_idx + 1:03d}/{len(train_loader):03d} | "
                f"Loss: {loss:.4f}"
            )

    ### Epoch-level logging
    model = model.eval()
    train_acc = compute_accuracy(model, train_loader, device)
    valid_acc = compute_accuracy(model, valid_loader, device)
    print(
        f"Training accuracy: {train_acc * 100:.2f}% | "
        f"Validation accuracy: {valid_acc * 100:.2f}%"
    )
    print(f"Time elapsed: {(time.time() - start_time) / 60:.2f} min")

cells.source: # Baseline -- Convolutional Neural Network on MNIST
## Imports

import os
import time

import numpy as np
import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F

if torch.cuda.is_available():
    torch.backends.cudnn.deterministic = True
## Settings

##########################
### SETTINGS
##########################

# Device
device = torch.device("cuda:0" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu")

# Hyperparameters
random_seed = 1
learning_rate = 0.001
num_epochs = 10
batch_size = 128

# Architecture
num_classes = 10
## Dataset
#!pip install gitpython

import os

from git import Repo

if not os.path.exists("mnist-pngs"):
    Repo.clone_from("https://github.com/rasbt/mnist-pngs", "mnist-pngs")

from torchvision import transforms

data_transforms = {
    "train": transforms.Compose(
        [
            transforms.Resize(32),
            transforms.RandomCrop((28, 28)),
            transforms.ToTensor(),
            # normalize images to [-1, 1] range
            transforms.Normalize((0.5, 0.5, 0.5), (0.5, 0.5, 0.5)),
        ]
    ),
    "test": transforms.Compose(
        [
            transforms.Resize(32),
            transforms.CenterCrop((28, 28)),
            transforms.ToTensor(),
            # normalize images to [-1, 1] range
            transforms.Normalize((0.5, 0.5, 0.5), (0.5, 0.5, 0.5)),
        ]
    ),
}

from torch.utils.data.dataset import random_split
from torchvision.datasets import ImageFolder

train_dset = ImageFolder(root="mnist-pngs/train", transform=data_transforms["train"])

train_dset, valid_dset = random_split(train_dset, lengths=[55000, 5000])

test_dset = ImageFolder(root="mnist-pngs/test", transform=data_transforms["test"])

from torch.utils.data import DataLoader

train_loader = DataLoader(
    dataset=train_dset,
    batch_size=batch_size,
    drop_last=True,
    num_workers=4,
    shuffle=True,
)

valid_loader = DataLoader(
    dataset=valid_dset,
    batch_size=batch_size,
    drop_last=False,
    num_workers=4,
    shuffle=False,
)

test_loader = DataLoader(
    dataset=test_dset,
    batch_size=batch_size,
    drop_last=False,
    num_workers=4,
    shuffle=False,
)

%matplotlib inline
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import torchvision.utils as vutils

real_batch = next(iter(train_loader))
plt.figure(figsize=(8, 8))
plt.axis("off")
plt.title("Training images")
plt.imshow(
    np.transpose(
        vutils.make_grid(real_batch[0][:64], padding=2, normalize=True), (1, 2, 0)
    )
)
plt.show()

cells.source: ## Model

import torch


class PyTorchCNN(torch.nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, num_classes):
        super().__init__()

        self.num_classes = num_classes
        self.features = torch.nn.Sequential(
            torch.nn.Conv2d(
                in_channels=3,
                out_channels=8,
                kernel_size=(3, 3),
                stride=(1, 1),
                padding=1,
            ),
            torch.nn.ReLU(),
            torch.nn.MaxPool2d(kernel_size=(2, 2), stride=(2, 2), padding=0),
            torch.nn.ReLU(),
            torch.nn.Conv2d(
                in_channels=8,
                out_channels=16,
                kernel_size=(3, 3),
                stride=(1, 1),
                padding=1,
            ),
            torch.nn.ReLU(),
            torch.nn.MaxPool2d(kernel_size=(2, 2), stride=(2, 2), padding=0),
        )

        self.classifier = torch.nn.Sequential(
            torch.nn.Flatten(),
            torch.nn.Linear(784, 128),
            torch.nn.ReLU(),
            torch.nn.Linear(128, num_classes),
        )

    def forward(self, x):
        x = self.features(x)
        x = self.classifier(x)
        return x


torch.manual_seed(random_seed)
model = PyTorchCNN(num_classes=num_classes)
model = model.to(device)
## Training

def compute_accuracy(model, data_loader, device):
    with torch.no_grad():
        correct_pred, num_examples = 0, 0
        for features, targets in data_loader:
            features, targets = features.to(device), targets.to(device)
            logits = model(features)
            _, predicted_labels = torch.max(logits, 1)
            num_examples += targets.size(0)
            correct_pred += (predicted_labels == targets).sum()
        return correct_pred.float() / num_examples

optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=learning_rate)

start_time = time.time()
for epoch in range(num_epochs):
    model = model.train()
    for batch_idx, (features, targets) in enumerate(train_loader):

        features, targets = features.to(device), targets.to(device)

        ### Forward pass
        logits = model(features)
        loss = F.cross_entropy(logits, targets)

        ### Backward pass (backpropagation)
        optimizer.zero_grad()
        loss.backward()

        ### Update model parameters
        optimizer.step()

        ### Batch-level logging
        if not (batch_idx + 1) % 100:
            print(
                f"Epoch: {epoch + 1:03d}/{num_epochs:03d} | "
                f"Batch: {batch_idx + 1:03d}/{len(train_loader):03d} | "
                f"Loss: {loss:.4f}"
            )

    ### Epoch-level logging
    model = model.eval()
    train_acc = compute_accuracy(model, train_loader, device)
    valid_acc = compute_accuracy(model, valid_loader, device)
    print(
        f"Training accuracy: {train_acc * 100:.2f}% | "
        f"Validation accuracy: {valid_acc * 100:.2f}%"
    )
    print(f"Time elapsed: {(time.time() - start_time) / 60:.2f} min")

print(f"Total training time: {(time.time() - start_time) / 60:.2f} min")

import torch


class PyTorchCNN(torch.nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, num_classes):
        super().__init__()

        self.num_classes = num_classes
        self.features = torch.nn.Sequential(
            torch.nn.Conv2d(
                in_channels=3,
                out_channels=8,
                kernel_size=(3, 3),
                stride=(1, 1),
                padding=1,
            ),
            torch.nn.ReLU(),
            torch.nn.MaxPool2d(kernel_size=(2, 2), stride=(2, 2), padding=0),
            torch.nn.ReLU(),
            torch.nn.Conv2d(
                in_channels=8,
                out_channels=16,
                kernel_size=(3, 3),
                stride=(1, 1),
                padding=1,
            ),
            torch.nn.ReLU(),
            torch.nn.MaxPool2d(kernel_size=(2, 2), stride=(2, 2), padding=0),
        )

        self.classifier = torch.nn.Sequential(
            torch.nn.Flatten(),
            torch.nn.Linear(784, 128),
            torch.nn.ReLU(),
            torch.nn.Linear(128, num_classes),
        )

    def forward(self, x):
        x = self.features(x)
        x = self.classifier(x)
        return x


torch.manual_seed(random_seed)
model = PyTorchCNN(num_classes=num_classes)
model = model.to(device)
## Training

def compute_accuracy(model, data_loader, device):
    with torch.no_grad():
        correct_pred, num_examples = 0, 0
        for features, targets in data_loader:
            features, targets = features.to(device), targets.to(device)
            logits = model(features)
            _, predicted_labels = torch.max(logits, 1)
            num_examples += targets.size(0)
            correct_pred += (predicted_labels == targets).sum()
        return correct_pred.float() / num_examples

optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=learning_rate)

start_time = time.time()
for epoch in range(num_epochs):
    model = model.train()
    for batch_idx, (features, targets) in enumerate(train_loader):

        features, targets = features.to(device), targets.to(device)

        ### Forward pass
        logits = model(features)
        loss = F.cross_entropy(logits, targets)

        ### Backward pass (backpropagation)
        optimizer.zero_grad()
        loss.backward()

        ### Update model parameters
        optimizer.step()

        ### Batch-level logging
        if not (batch_idx + 1) % 100:
            print(
                f"Epoch: {epoch + 1:03d}/{num_epochs:03d} | "
                f"Batch: {batch_idx + 1:03d}/{len(train_loader):03d} | "
                f"Loss: {loss:.4f}"
            )

    ### Epoch-level logging
    model = model.eval()
    train_acc = compute_accuracy(model, train_loader, device)
    valid_acc = compute_accuracy(model, valid_loader, device)
    print(
        f"Training accuracy: {train_acc * 100:.2f}% | "
        f"Validation accuracy: {valid_acc * 100:.2f}%"
    )
    print(f"Time elapsed: {(time.time() - start_time) / 60:.2f} min")

print(f"Total training time: {(time.time() - start_time) / 60:.2f} min")

1	# 评估工具链：准确率、混淆矩阵与失败案例
2	
3	## 1. 本讲目标
4	
5	学完本讲，你应该能够：
6	
7	1. 用仓库共享的 `compute_confusion_matrix` 计算混淆矩阵，并用 `plot_confusion_matrix` 把它画成带数字标注的热力图，从矩阵直接读出「模型最常把谁认成谁」。
8	2. 用 `show_examples` 展示一批「预测值 vs 真实值」对照的样本图片，并在此基础上编写自己的「只展示误分类样本」函数。
9	3. 说清 torchmetrics 中 `.update()` 与 `.forward()`（即 `__call__`）两种调用方式的语义差异：为什么前者返回 `None`、后者返回当前 batch 的指标值，而两者最终的 `.compute()` 结果完全一致；并掌握「分子/分母分别累计」这一指标累计的正确姿势。
10	
11	本讲是第 7 单元（训练评估与技巧）的第一讲。上一单元你已经把训练循环交给了 `helper_train` 的共享工具链（u4-l4），本讲把「训练完之后怎么评估、怎么诊断错误」这块拼图补齐。
12	
13	## 2. 前置知识
14	
15	本讲默认你已完成 u4-l4（公共训练评估工具链与确定性），以下概念直接沿用，不再重复展开：
16	
17	- **五步训练范式**：forward → loss → zero_grad → backward → step；评估阶段则统一在 `model.eval()` + `torch.no_grad()` 下进行。
18	- **`compute_accuracy` / `compute_epoch_loss`**：`helper_evaluate.py` 中的一对评估函数，前者内部自带 `eval()` 与 `no_grad()`，后者用 `reduction='sum'` 先求和再除以样本数。
19	- **`log_dict` 与最优 checkpoint**：`train_classifier_simple_v1/v2` 返回的训练日志；报告成绩前应重载最优 checkpoint。
20	- **`UnNormalize`**（u4-l3）：标准化张量直接画图会失真，须乘 `std` 加 `mean` 还原到 [0,1] 再交给 matplotlib。
21	
22	本讲新引入的术语，先用一段话建立直觉：
23	
24	- **混淆矩阵（confusion matrix）**：一个 K×K 的表格，第 i 行第 j 列存放「真实标签为 i、被预测成 j」的样本数。对角线是预测正确的样本，非对角线格子则是「失败案例」的聚集地。准确率只告诉你「错了多少」，混淆矩阵还告诉你「错成了什么」。
25	- **行归一化（row normalization）**：把每一行除以该行总和，得到「真实类别 i 的样本中被预测为 j 的比例」。对角线上的归一化值就是类别 i 的召回率（recall）。
26	- **torchmetrics**：一个把「指标累计」封装成对象的库。你创建一个 `Accuracy()` 对象，逐 batch 喂数据，最后一次性 `.compute()`。它的核心价值是：不需要把所有预测堆在内存里，只需要累计少量统计量（正确数、样本数）。
27	
28	## 3. 本讲源码地图
29	
30	| 文件 | 作用 |
31	| --- | --- |
32	| `pytorch_ipynb/helper_evaluate.py` | 评估指标函数库：`compute_accuracy`、`compute_epoch_loss`、`compute_confusion_matrix` |
33	| `pytorch_ipynb/helper_plotting.py` | 可视化函数库：`plot_training_loss`、`plot_accuracy`、`show_examples`、`plot_confusion_matrix` |
34	| `pytorch_ipynb/helper_data.py` | `UnNormalize` 类所在的共享模块，`show_examples` 的反标准化参数由它构造（本讲只用到这一个类） |
35	| `pytorch_ipynb/related-libraries/torchmetrics-update-forward.ipynb` | 作者写的 torchmetrics 专题 notebook：用 10 个模拟 minibatch 对比手工计算、`.update()`、`.forward()` 三种方式 |
36	| `pytorch_ipynb/cnn/cnn-mobilenet-v3-small-cifar10.ipynb` | 仓库中真实调用这套评估工具链的范例 notebook，本讲引用它的 Evaluation 段作为「标准用法」 |
37	
38	注意引用方式：这些 notebook 都通过 `sys.path.insert(0, "..")` 把 `pytorch_ipynb/` 目录加入搜索路径后再 `from helper_evaluate import ...`（[pytorch_ipynb/cnn/cnn-mobilenet-v3-small-cifar10.ipynb:L71-L79](https://github.com/rasbt/deeplearning-models/blob/59beda3aa25337e576564f1c18c6edd26f9f30e3/pytorch_ipynb/cnn/cnn-mobilenet-v3-small-cifar10.ipynb#L71-L79)）。你在自己的 notebook 里复现时也要保证能找到这两个 helper 文件。
39	
40	## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解
41	
42	本讲的三个最小模块：**混淆矩阵**、**样本展示工具**、**torchmetrics 指标**。
43	
44	### 4.1 混淆矩阵：从 `compute_confusion_matrix` 到 `plot_confusion_matrix`
45	
46	#### 4.1.1 概念说明
47	
48	准确率是一个把所有信息压缩成单个数字的指标：\[ \text{Accuracy} = \frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^{N} \mathbb{1}[\hat{y}_n = y_n] \] 它回答「平均对了多少」，但掩盖了错误的结构。比如 MNIST 上 97.5% 的准确率，剩下的 2.5% 错误可能集中在「4 认成 9」「3 认成 5」这几对形近数字上——这正是改进模型时最该先知道的信息。
49	
50	混淆矩阵把这些错误结构完整保留下来：\[ C_{ij} = \sum_{n=1}^{N} \mathbb{1}[y_n = i,\ \hat{y}_n = j] \] 约定**行是真实标签、列是预测标签**（仓库的 `plot_confusion_matrix` 在坐标轴上明确标注了这一点）。于是：
51	
52	- 对角线元素之和 = 预测正确的样本总数，除以 N 就是准确率——混淆矩阵是准确率的「无损上游」。
53	- 每一行除以行和得到行归一化矩阵 \(\tilde{C}_{ij} = C_{ij} / \sum_j C_{ij}\)，其第 i 行对角线值即类别 i 的召回率。
54	
55	#### 4.1.2 核心流程
56	
57	`compute_confusion_matrix(model, data_loader, device)` 的执行过程：
58	
59	1. 准备两个空列表 `all_targets`、`all_predictions`。
60	2. 在 `torch.no_grad()` 下遍历整个 data_loader：前向得到 logits，`torch.max(logits, 1)` 取预测标签，把 targets 与预测标签逐 batch 搬到 CPU 后 `extend` 进列表。
61	3. 两个列表转成 NumPy 数组。
62	4. 用 `np.unique` 在「真实标签 ∪ 预测标签」上取类别集合，处理「只出现一个类别」的退化情形。
63	5. 用 `itertools.product` 枚举所有 (真实, 预测) 类别组合，统计每对组合的出现次数。
64	6. 把长度为 K² 的计数列表 reshape 成 K×K 矩阵返回。
65	
66	随后 `plot_confusion_matrix(conf_mat, ...)` 负责画图：行归一化 → `matshow` 热力图 → 每格写上绝对计数（可选加归一化比例）→ 贴类别名。
67	
68	#### 4.1.3 源码精读
69	
70	**第一步：收集全部预测。** [pytorch_ipynb/helper_evaluate.py:L43-L55](https://github.com/rasbt/deeplearning-models/blob/59beda3aa25337e576564f1c18c6edd26f9f30e3/pytorch_ipynb/helper_evaluate.py#L43-L55) 中，函数在 `no_grad` 下逐 batch 前向，`torch.max(logits, 1)` 沿类别维取 argmax，随后把 targets 与预测标签都搬到 CPU 再 extend——注意这一步与 `compute_accuracy` 不同：混淆矩阵必须**保留每个样本的 (真实, 预测) 对**，不能在循环内就地累加，所以这里选择了「先收集、后统计」的方案。
71	
72	**第二步：确定类别集合与退化处理。** [pytorch_ipynb/helper_evaluate.py:L57-L67](https://github.com/rasbt/deeplearning-models/blob/59beda3aa25337e576564f1c18c6edd26f9f30e3/pytorch_ipynb/helper_evaluate.py#L57-L67) 把列表转 NumPy 数组，用 `np.unique(np.concatenate((all_targets, all_predictions)))` 取类别标签。两个细节值得注意：
73	
74	- 类别集合取自「真实 ∪ 预测」的并集，因此矩阵维度由实际出现的标签决定，而不是硬编码 10；
75	- 若并集里只有一个类别（比如二分类任务恰好全部预测正确且只出现一个标签），L62-L66 会补一个 0 或 1 凑成 2×2，避免产出 1×1 的「假矩阵」。
76	
77	**第三步：暴力计数。** [pytorch_ipynb/helper_evaluate.py:L68-L73](https://github.com/rasbt/deeplearning-models/blob/59beda3aa25337e576564f1c18c6edd26f9f30e3/pytorch_ipynb/helper_evaluate.py#L68-L73) 是这个函数最有教学价值的一段：先把 (target, prediction) 打包成元组列表 `z`，再用 `product(class_labels, repeat=2)` 按行主序枚举所有 (i, j) 组合，用 `z.count(combi)` 数出现次数，最后 reshape 成 K×K。`product` 的枚举顺序是 (c₀,c₀), (c₀,c₁), …, (c₁,c₀), …，与 reshape 的行主序一致，所以**第 i 行对应真实标签 i、第 j 列对应预测标签 j**。这种写法是 O(K²·N) 的暴力扫描（K 是类别数），对 MNIST/CIFAR 的 10 类、万级样本完全够用；生产环境通常会换成一维 `np.bincount` 式向量化计数，但教学上「直接数元组出现次数」最透明。
78	
79	**第四步：画图。** [pytorch_ipynb/helper_plotting.py:L130-L137](https://github.com/rasbt/deeplearning-models/blob/59beda3aa25337e576564f1c18c6edd26f9f30e3/pytorch_ipynb/helper_plotting.py#L130-L137) 先做参数断言（两种显示模式不能同时关闭；`class_names` 长度必须等于矩阵维度），随后 `conf_mat.sum(axis=1)[:, np.newaxis]` 沿**行方向**求和——每行总和即真实类别 i 的样本数——再相除得到行归一化矩阵。也就是说，归一化基准是「每个真实类别的样本数」，归一化后的第 i 行是类别 i 的样本被分到各类的比例。
80	
81	[pytorch_ipynb/helper_plotting.py:L147-L171](https://github.com/rasbt/deeplearning-models/blob/59beda3aa25337e576564f1c18c6edd26f9f30e3/pytorch_ipynb/helper_plotting.py#L147-L171) 决定「画什么、写什么」：`show_normed` 控制用绝对计数还是归一化矩阵喂给 `matshow`（默认 `plt.cm.Blues` 色表）；双重循环给每个格子写注释——绝对计数总是整数格式，若同时开启 `show_absolute` 与 `show_normed` 则在数字下方追加括号里的两位小数比例。L171 有个贴心细节：格子归一化值超过 0.5（底色已很深）时文字用白色，否则用黑色，保证任何底色上文字都可读。
82	
83	**第五步：坐标轴与返回值。** [pytorch_ipynb/helper_plotting.py:L173-L191](https://github.com/rasbt/deeplearning-models/blob/59beda3aa25337e576564f1c18c6edd26f9f30e3/pytorch_ipynb/helper_plotting.py#L173-L191) 用 `class_names` 设置刻度（x 轴刻度旋转 90 度），最后 `plt.xlabel('predicted label')` / `plt.ylabel('true label')` 明确了行列语义，并 `return fig, ax`——返回画布对象而不是内部 `plt.show()`，方便调用方进一步定制或保存。
84	
85	**仓库中的标准用法**（MobileNet-v3-small 在 CIFAR-10 上的 Evaluation 段）：[pytorch_ipynb/cnn/cnn-mobilenet-v3-small-cifar10.ipynb:L1289-L1291](https://github.com/rasbt/deeplearning-models/blob/59beda3aa25337e576564f1c18c6edd26f9f30e3/pytorch_ipynb/cnn/cnn-mobilenet-v3-small-cifar10.ipynb#L1289-L1291) 先 `model.cpu()`，再一行算矩阵、一行画图：
86	
87	```python
88	mat = compute_confusion_matrix(model=model, data_loader=test_loader, device=torch.device('cpu'))
89	plot_confusion_matrix(mat, class_names=class_dict.values())
90	plt.show()
91	```
92	
93	#### 4.1.4 代码实践
94	
95	**实践目标**：验证「混淆矩阵的对角线之和除以总数 = `compute_accuracy` 的返回值」，亲手确认混淆矩阵是准确率的无损上游。
96	
97	**操作步骤**：
98	
99	1. 挑一个你已经训练好的模型（推荐复用 u2-l3 的 `mlp-basic` 或 u3-l1 的 `cnn-basic`，任一 MNIST 模型均可），把本讲源码地图中的 import 段抄到 notebook 里。
100	2. 运行下面的对账代码（示例代码）：
101	
102	```python
103	import torch, numpy as np
104	from helper_evaluate import compute_accuracy, compute_confusion_matrix
105	from helper_plotting import plot_confusion_matrix
106	import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
107	
108	test_acc = compute_accuracy(model, test_loader, device)          # 百分比
109	mat = compute_confusion_matrix(model, test_loader, device)       # 10x10 numpy 数组
110	
111	acc_from_mat = np.trace(mat) / mat.sum() * 100
112	print(f'compute_accuracy : {test_acc:.2f}%')
113	print(f'对角线/总数     : {acc_from_mat:.2f}%')
114	
115	plot_confusion_matrix(mat, class_names=[str(i) for i in range(10)],
116	                      show_normed=True, figsize=(8, 8))
117	plt.show()
118	```
119	
120	3. 找出混淆最严重的一对类别：对非对角线元素做 `np.unravel_index(mat.argmax() ...)` 前先把对角线置零（示例代码）：

# 评估工具链：准确率、混淆矩阵与失败案例

## 1. 本讲目标

学完本讲，你应该能够：

1. 用仓库共享的 `compute_confusion_matrix` 计算混淆矩阵，并用 `plot_confusion_matrix` 把它画成带数字标注的热力图，从矩阵直接读出「模型最常把谁认成谁」。
2. 用 `show_examples` 展示一批「预测值 vs 真实值」对照的样本图片，并在此基础上编写自己的「只展示误分类样本」函数。
3. 说清 torchmetrics 中 `.update()` 与 `.forward()`（即 `__call__`）两种调用方式的语义差异：为什么前者返回 `None`、后者返回当前 batch 的指标值，而两者最终的 `.compute()` 结果完全一致；并掌握「分子/分母分别累计」这一指标累计的正确姿势。

本讲是第 7 单元（训练评估与技巧）的第一讲。上一单元你已经把训练循环交给了 `helper_train` 的共享工具链（u4-l4），本讲把「训练完之后怎么评估、怎么诊断错误」这块拼图补齐。

## 2. 前置知识

本讲默认你已完成 u4-l4（公共训练评估工具链与确定性），以下概念直接沿用，不再重复展开：

- **五步训练范式**：forward → loss → zero_grad → backward → step；评估阶段则统一在 `model.eval()` + `torch.no_grad()` 下进行。
- **`compute_accuracy` / `compute_epoch_loss`**：`helper_evaluate.py` 中的一对评估函数，前者内部自带 `eval()` 与 `no_grad()`，后者用 `reduction='sum'` 先求和再除以样本数。
- **`log_dict` 与最优 checkpoint**：`train_classifier_simple_v1/v2` 返回的训练日志；报告成绩前应重载最优 checkpoint。
- **`UnNormalize`**（u4-l3）：标准化张量直接画图会失真，须乘 `std` 加 `mean` 还原到 [0,1] 再交给 matplotlib。

本讲新引入的术语，先用一段话建立直觉：

- **混淆矩阵（confusion matrix）**：一个 K×K 的表格，第 i 行第 j 列存放「真实标签为 i、被预测成 j」的样本数。对角线是预测正确的样本，非对角线格子则是「失败案例」的聚集地。准确率只告诉你「错了多少」，混淆矩阵还告诉你「错成了什么」。
- **行归一化（row normalization）**：把每一行除以该行总和，得到「真实类别 i 的样本中被预测为 j 的比例」。对角线上的归一化值就是类别 i 的召回率（recall）。
- **torchmetrics**：一个把「指标累计」封装成对象的库。你创建一个 `Accuracy()` 对象，逐 batch 喂数据，最后一次性 `.compute()`。它的核心价值是：不需要把所有预测堆在内存里，只需要累计少量统计量（正确数、样本数）。

## 3. 本讲源码地图

| 文件 | 作用 |
| --- | --- |
| `pytorch_ipynb/helper_evaluate.py` | 评估指标函数库：`compute_accuracy`、`compute_epoch_loss`、`compute_confusion_matrix` |
| `pytorch_ipynb/helper_plotting.py` | 可视化函数库：`plot_training_loss`、`plot_accuracy`、`show_examples`、`plot_confusion_matrix` |

## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解

本讲的三个最小模块：**混淆矩阵**、**样本展示工具**、**torchmetrics 指标**。

### 4.1 混淆矩阵：从 `compute_confusion_matrix` 到 `plot_confusion_matrix`

#### 4.1.1 概念说明

准确率是一个把所有信息压缩成单个数字的指标：\[ \text{Accuracy} = \frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^{N} \mathbb{1}[\hat{y}_n = y_n] \] 它回答「平均对了多少」，但掩盖了错误的结构。比如 MNIST 上 97.5% 的准确率，剩下的 2.5% 错误可能集中在「4 认成 9」「3 认成 5」这几对形近数字上——这正是改进模型时最该先知道的信息。

混淆矩阵把这些错误结构完整保留下来：\[ C_{ij} = \sum_{n=1}^{N} \mathbb{1}[y_n = i,\ \hat{y}_n = j] \] 约定**行是真实标签、列是预测标签**（仓库的 `plot_confusion_matrix` 在坐标轴上明确标注了这一点）。于是：

- 对角线元素之和 = 预测正确的样本总数，除以 N 就是准确率——混淆矩阵是准确率的「无损上游」。
- 每一行除以行和得到行归一化矩阵 \(\tilde{C}_{ij} = C_{ij} / \sum_j C_{ij}\)，其第 i 行对角线值即类别 i 的召回率。

#### 4.1.2 核心流程

`compute_confusion_matrix(model, data_loader, device)` 的执行过程：

1. 准备两个空列表 `all_targets`、`all_predictions`。
2. 在 `torch.no_grad()` 下遍历整个 data_loader：前向得到 logits，`torch.max(logits, 1)` 取预测标签，把 targets 与预测标签逐 batch 搬到 CPU 后 `extend` 进列表。
3. 两个列表转成 NumPy 数组。
4. 用 `np.unique` 在「真实标签 ∪ 预测标签」上取类别集合，处理「只出现一个类别」的退化情形。
5. 用 `itertools.product` 枚举所有 (真实, 预测) 类别组合，统计每对组合的出现次数。
6. 把长度为 K² 的计数列表 reshape 成 K×K 矩阵返回。

随后 `plot_confusion_matrix(conf_mat, ...)` 负责画图：行归一化 → `matshow` 热力图 → 每格写上绝对计数（可选加归一化比例）→ 贴类别名。

#### 4.1.3 源码精读

**第一步：收集全部预测。** [pytorch_ipynb/helper_evaluate.py:L43-L55](https://github.com/rasbt/deeplearning-models/blob/59beda3aa25337e576564f1c18c6edd26f9f30e3/pytorch_ipynb/helper_evaluate.py#L43-L55) 中，函数在 `no_grad` 下逐 batch 前向，`torch.max(logits, 1)` 沿类别维取 argmax，随后把 targets 与预测标签都搬到 CPU 再 extend——注意这一步与 `compute_accuracy` 不同：混淆矩阵必须**保留每个样本的 (真实, 预测) 对**，不能在循环内就地累加，所以这里选择了「先收集、后统计」的方案。

**第二步：确定类别集合与退化处理。** [pytorch_ipynb/helper_evaluate.py:L57-L67](https://github.com/rasbt/deeplearning-models/blob/59beda3aa25337e576564f1c18c6edd26f9f30e3/pytorch_ipynb/helper_evaluate.py#L57-L67) 把列表转 NumPy 数组，用 `np.unique(np.concatenate((all_targets, all_predictions)))` 取类别标签。两个细节值得注意：

- 类别集合取自「真实 ∪ 预测」的并集，因此矩阵维度由实际出现的标签决定，而不是硬编码 10；
- 若并集里只有一个类别（比如二分类任务恰好全部预测正确且只出现一个标签），L62-L66 会补一个 0 或 1 凑成 2×2，避免产出 1×1 的「假矩阵」。

**第三步：暴力计数。** [pytorch_ipynb/helper_evaluate.py:L68-L73](https://github.com/rasbt/deeplearning-models/blob/59beda3aa25337e576564f1c18c6edd26f9f30e3/pytorch_ipynb/helper_evaluate.py#L68-L73) 是这个函数最有教学价值的一段：先把 (target, prediction) 打包成元组列表 `z`，再用 `product(class_labels, repeat=2)` 按行主序枚举所有 (i, j) 组合，用 `z.count(combi)` 数出现次数，最后 reshape 成 K×K。`product` 的枚举顺序是 (c₀,c₀), (c₀,c₁), …, (c₁,c₀), …，与 reshape 的行主序一致，所以**第 i 行对应真实标签 i、第 j 列对应预测标签 j**。这种写法是 O(K²·N) 的暴力扫描（K 是类别数），对 MNIST/CIFAR 的 10 类、万级样本完全够用；生产环境通常会换成一维 `np.bincount` 式向量化计数，但教学上「直接数元组出现次数」最透明。

**第四步：画图。** [pytorch_ipynb/helper_plotting.py:L130-L137](https://github.com/rasbt/deeplearning-models/blob/59beda3aa25337e576564f1c18c6edd26f9f30e3/pytorch_ipynb/helper_plotting.py#L130-L137) 先做参数断言（两种显示模式不能同时关闭；`class_names` 长度必须等于矩阵维度），随后 `conf_mat.sum(axis=1)[:, np.newaxis]` 沿**行方向**求和——每行总和即真实类别 i 的样本数——再相除得到行归一化矩阵。也就是说，归一化基准是「每个真实类别的样本数」，归一化后的第 i 行是类别 i 的样本被分到各类的比例。

[pytorch_ipynb/helper_plotting.py:L147-L171](https://github.com/rasbt/deeplearning-models/blob/59beda3aa25337e576564f1c18c6edd26f9f30e3/pytorch_ipynb/helper_plotting.py#L147-L171) 决定「画什么、写什么」：`show_normed` 控制用绝对计数还是归一化矩阵喂给 `matshow`（默认 `plt.cm.Blues` 色表）；双重循环给每个格子写注释——绝对计数总是整数格式，若同时开启 `show_absolute` 与 `show_normed` 则在数字下方追加括号里的两位小数比例。L171 有个贴心细节：格子归一化值超过 0.5（底色已很深）时文字用白色，否则用黑色，保证任何底色上文字都可读。

**第五步：坐标轴与返回值。** [pytorch_ipynb/helper_plotting.py:L173-L191](https://github.com/rasbt/deeplearning-models/blob/59beda3aa25337e576564f1c18c6edd26f9f30e3/pytorch_ipynb/helper_plotting.py#L173-L191) 用 `class_names` 设置刻度（x 轴刻度旋转 90 度），最后 `plt.xlabel('predicted label')` / `plt.ylabel('true label')` 明确了行列语义，并 `return fig, ax`——返回画布对象而不是内部 `plt.show()`，方便调用方进一步定制或保存。

**仓库中的标准用法**（MobileNet-v3-small 在 CIFAR-10 上的 Evaluation 段）：[pytorch_ipynb/cnn/cnn-mobilenet-v3-small-cifar10.ipynb:L1289-L1291](https://github.com/rasbt/deeplearning-models/blob/59beda3aa25337e576564f1c18c6edd26f9f30e3/pytorch_ipynb/cnn/cnn-mobilenet-v3-small-cifar10.ipynb#L1289-L1291) 先 `model.cpu()`，再一行算矩阵、一行画图：

<cell id="cell-23">import torch


class PyTorchCNN(torch.nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, num_classes):
        super().__init__()

        self.num_classes = num_classes
        self.features = torch.nn.Sequential(
            torch.nn.Conv2d(
                in_channels=3,
                out_channels=8,
                kernel_size=(3, 3),
                stride=(1, 1),
                padding=1,
            ),
            torch.nn.ReLU(),
            torch.nn.MaxPool2d(kernel_size=(2, 2), stride=(2, 2), padding=0),
            torch.nn.ReLU(),
            torch.nn.Conv2d(
                in_channels=8,
                out_channels=16,
                kernel_size=(3, 3),
                stride=(1, 1),
                padding=1,
            ),
            torch.nn.ReLU(),
            torch.nn.MaxPool2d(kernel_size=(2, 2), stride=(2, 2), padding=0),
        )

        self.classifier = torch.nn.Sequential(
            torch.nn.Flatten(),
            torch.nn.Linear(784, 128),
            torch.nn.ReLU(),
            torch.nn.Linear(128, num_classes),
        )

    def forward(self, x):
        x = self.features(x)
        x = self.classifier(x)
        return x</cell id="cell-23">
<cell id="cell-24">import pytorch_lightning as pl
import torchmetrics


# LightningModule that receives a PyTorch model as input
class LightningModel(pl.LightningModule):
    def __init__(self, model, learning_rate):
        super().__init__()

        self.learning_rate = learning_rate
        # The inherited PyTorch module
        self.model = model

        # Save settings and hyperparameters to the log directory
        # but skip the model parameters
        self.save_hyperparameters(ignore=["model"])

        # Set up attributes for computing the accuracy
        self.train_acc = torchmetrics.Accuracy()
        self.valid_acc = torchmetrics.Accuracy()
        self.test_acc = torchmetrics.Accuracy()

    # Defining the forward method is only necessary
    # if you want to use a Trainer's .predict() method (optional)
    def forward(self, x):
        return self.model(x)

    # A common forward step to compute the loss and labels
    # this is used for training, validation, and testing below
    def _shared_step(self, batch):
        features, true_labels = batch
        logits = self(features)
        loss = torch.nn.functional.cross_entropy(logits, true_labels)
        predicted_labels = torch.argmax(logits, dim=1)

        return loss, true_labels, predicted_labels

    def training_step(self, batch, batch_idx):
        loss, true_labels, predicted_labels = self._shared_step(batch)
        self.log("train_loss", loss)

        # To account for Dropout behavior during evaluation
        self.model.eval()
        with torch.no_grad():
            _, true_labels, predicted_labels = self._shared_step(batch)
        self.train_acc.update(predicted_labels, true_labels)
        self.log("train_acc", self.train_acc, on_epoch=True, on_step=False)
        self.model.train()
        return loss  # this is passed to the optimzer for training

    def validation_step(self, batch, batch_idx):
        loss, true_labels, predicted_labels = self._shared_step(batch)
        self.log("valid_loss", loss)
        self.valid_acc(predicted_labels, true_labels)
        self.log(
            "valid_acc", self.valid_acc, on_epoch=True, on_step=False, prog_bar=True
        )

    def test_step(self, batch, batch_idx):
        loss, true_labels, predicted_labels = self._shared_step(batch)
        self.test_acc(predicted_labels, true_labels)
        self.log("test_acc", self.test_acc, on_epoch=True, on_step=False)

    def configure_optimizers(self):
        optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(self.parameters(), lr=self.learning_rate)
        return optimizer</cell id="cell-24">

# K-Fold Cross-Validation Example -- Convolutional Neural Network on MNIST

This notebook shows how to apply k-fold cross-validation to deep neural networks using PyTorch Lightning and [`pl_cross`](https://github.com/SkafteNicki/pl_cross).

This notebook is based on a basic PyTorch Lightning notebook at [./baseline-cnn-mnist.ipynb](baseline-cnn-mnist.ipynb). The changes are annotated and/or highlighted.
## Imports

import os
import time

import numpy as np
import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F

if torch.cuda.is_available():
    torch.backends.cudnn.deterministic = True
## Settings

##########################
### SETTINGS
##########################

# Hyperparameters
RANDOM_SEED = 1
LEARNING_RATE = 0.001
NUM_EPOCHS = 10
BATCH_SIZE = 128

# Architecture
NUM_CLASSES = 10
## NEW: Install `pl_cross` Library
Uncomment the following line if you don't have Git Python installed yet.

from git import Repo

if not os.path.exists("pl_cross"):
    Repo.clone_from("https://github.com/SkafteNicki/pl_cross.git", "pl_cross")
Uncomment the following line to install the cloned repo.

## Dataset

if not os.path.exists("mnist-pngs"):
    Repo.clone_from("https://github.com/rasbt/mnist-pngs", "mnist-pngs")

from torchvision import transforms

data_transforms = {
    "train": transforms.Compose(
        [
            transforms.Resize(32),
            transforms.RandomCrop((28, 28)),
            transforms.ToTensor(),
            # normalize images to [-1, 1] range
            transforms.Normalize((0.5, 0.5, 0.5), (0.5, 0.5, 0.5)),

    ),
    "test": transforms.Compose(
        [
            transforms.Resize(32),
            transforms.CenterCrop((28, 28)),
            transforms.ToTensor(),
            # normalize images to [-1, 1] range
            transforms.Normalize((0.5, 0.5, 0.5), (0.5, 0.5, 0.5)),
        ]
    ),
}

from torch.utils.data.dataset import random_split
from torchvision.datasets import ImageFolder

train_dset = ImageFolder(root="mnist-pngs/train", transform=data_transforms["train"])

train_dset, valid_dset = random_split(train_dset, lengths=[55000, 5000])

test_dset = ImageFolder(root="mnist-pngs/test", transform=data_transforms["test"])

cells.source: ## Model
The model setup is exactly as it is before, except that the current k-fold code won't be using `validation_step`. We can still leave it in the `LightningModule` as it doesn't hurt either.

import torch


class PyTorchCNN(torch.nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, num_classes):
        super().__init__()

        self.num_classes = num_classes
        self.features = torch.nn.Sequential(
            torch.nn.Conv2d(
                in_channels=3,
                out_channels=8,
                kernel_size=(3, 3),
                stride=(1, 1),
                padding=1,
            ),
            torch.nn.ReLU(),
            torch.nn.MaxPool2d(kernel_size=(2, 2), stride=(2, 2), padding=0),
            torch.nn.ReLU(),
            torch.nn.Conv2d(
                in_channels=8,
                out_channels=16,
                kernel_size=(3, 3),
                stride=(1, 1),
                padding=1,
            ),
            torch.nn.ReLU(),
            torch.nn.MaxPool2d(kernel_size=(2, 2), stride=(2, 2), padding=0),
        )

        self.classifier = torch.nn.Sequential(
            torch.nn.Flatten(),
            torch.nn.Linear(784, 128),
            torch.nn.ReLU(),
            torch.nn.Linear(128, num_classes),
        )

    def forward(self, x):
        x = self.features(x)
        x = self.classifier(x)
        return x

import pytorch_lightning as pl
import torchmetrics


# LightningModule that receives a PyTorch model as input
class LightningModel(pl.LightningModule):
    def __init__(self, model, learning_rate):
        super().__init__()

        self.learning_rate = learning_rate
        # The inherited PyTorch module
        self.model = model

        # Save settings and hyperparameters to the log directory
        # but skip the model parameters
        self.save_hyperparameters(ignore=["model"])

        # Set up attributes for computing the accuracy
        self.train_acc = torchmetrics.Accuracy()
        self.valid_acc = torchmetrics.Accuracy()
        self.test_acc = torchmetrics.Accuracy()

    # Defining the forward method is only necessary
    # if you want to use a Trainer's .predict() method (optional)
    def forward(self, x):
        return self.model(x)

    # A common forward step to compute the loss and labels
    # this is used for training, validation, and testing below
    def _shared_step(self, batch):
        features, true_labels = batch
        logits = self(features)
        loss = torch.nn.functional.cross_entropy(logits, true_labels)
        predicted_labels = torch.argmax(logits, dim=1)

        return loss, true_labels, predicted_labels

    def training_step(self, batch, batch_idx):
        loss, true_labels, predicted_labels = self._shared_step(batch)
        self.log("train_loss", loss)

        # To account for Dropout behavior during evaluation
        self.model.eval()
        with torch.no_grad():
            _, true_labels, predicted_labels = self._shared_step(batch)
        self.train_acc.update(predicted_labels, true_labels)
        self.log("train_acc", self.train_acc, on_epoch=True, on_step=False)
        self.model.train()
        return loss  # this is passed to the optimzer for training

    def validation_step(self, batch, batch_idx):
        loss, true_labels, predicted_labels = self._shared_step(batch)
        self.log("valid_loss", loss)
        self.valid_acc(predicted_labels, true_labels)
        self.log(
            "valid_acc", self.valid_acc, on_epoch=True, on_step=False, prog_bar=True
        )

    def test_step(self, batch, batch_idx):
        loss, true_labels, predicted_labels = self._shared_step(batch)
        self.test_acc(predicted_labels, true_labels)
        self.log("test_acc", self.test_acc, on_epoch=True, on_step=False)

    def configure_optimizers(self):
        optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(self.parameters(), lr=self.learning_rate)
        return optimizer
## Training

NEW: Note that for logging, we need to import a modified version of the logger from the `pl_cross` library. Also, since the k-fold approach doesn't use `validation_step` we can't checkpoint based on teh validation set accuracy and have the `training_accuracy` instead.

# OLD:
# from pytorch_lightning.loggers import CSVLogger
# NEW:
from pl_cross.loggers import CSVLogger
from pytorch_lightning.callbacks import ModelCheckpoint

torch.manual_seed(RANDOM_SEED)
pytorch_model = PyTorchCNN(num_classes=NUM_CLASSES)

lightning_model = LightningModel(model=pytorch_model, learning_rate=LEARNING_RATE)


# NEW: Kfold currently doesn't call model.validation_step()
# so the valid_acc tracking does unfortunately not work, and
# we have to change valid_acc to train_acc.

callbacks = [
    ModelCheckpoint(save_top_k=1, mode="max", monitor="train_acc"),  # save top 1 model
    pl.callbacks.progress.TQDMProgressBar(refresh_rate=50),
]

logger = CSVLogger(save_dir="logs/", name="my-kfold-model")
NEW: Instead of using `pl.Trainer`, we use the `Trainer` from the `pl_cross` library, which lets us specify the number of folds as shown below:

import time

# NEW:
from pl_cross import Trainer

trainer = Trainer(
    num_folds=5,
    shuffle=True,
    # stratified=True,
    max_epochs=NUM_EPOCHS,
    callbacks=callbacks,
    accelerator="auto",  # Uses GPUs or TPUs if available
    devices="auto",  # Uses all available GPUs/TPUs if applicable
    logger=logger,
    log_every_n_steps=100,
)

start_time = time.time()

# NEW
kfold_results = trainer.cross_validate(
    model=lightning_model,
    train_dataloader=train_loader,
)

runtime = (time.time() - start_time) / 60
print(f"Training took {runtime:.2f} min in total.")
